\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Compression Step}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.CompressionStep
\section{Overview}

This module collects helper lemmas for the layer-reduction step of the LMN argument.
It handles the base case where the top circuit is a single literal, applies the
switching lemma to bound decision-tree depth under a random restriction, and shows how
the switched gates can be repackaged as clean, bounded-width DNFs.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Depth-zero circuits are literals]
\lean{LMN.circuit_depth_zero_is_lit}
\label{LMN.circuit_depth_zero_is_lit}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit, BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Lit}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m$ variables — a tree whose leaves are literals and
whose internal nodes are AND or OR gates applied to lists of subcircuits — and suppose
its depth is $0$. Then $c$ is a single leaf: there exists a literal $l$ such that $c$
consists of that literal alone.
\end{lemma}

\uses{BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit, BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.depth, BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.eval, BoolCircuit.TreeCircuit.size, BoolCircuit.Lit, DNF.eval, LMN.Layer2Data, LMN.circuit_depth_zero_is_lit, LMN.composedDelta, LMN.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_dnf_general, SwitchingLemma.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma.restrictFn, dtDepth, dtDepth_neg}
\difficulty{5}
Let $g_1,\dots,g_m$ be DNF formulas on $n$ Boolean variables, and let $w$ be a positive
integer such that every $g_i$ has width at most $w$; assume $n \ge 1$, and that in each
term the literals occupy distinct positions and any two literals sharing a variable are
equal (so each variable is queried at most once per term). Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit
on the $m$ gate-inputs whose depth is $0$ (hence a single literal), and let $F$ be the
composed Boolean function on $n$ variables given by $F(x) =
c\bigl(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\bigr)$. Fix natural numbers $s$, $l$, $t$ with $l \ge 1$, $s
\ge 1$, $w \le l$, and $\mathrm{size}(c) \le s$. Then, for a Bernoulli random
restriction $\rho$ with parameter $\tfrac{1}{40l}$, the probability that the restriction
of $F$ along $\rho$ — the function sending $x$ to $F$ evaluated with the coordinates
fixed by $\rho$ and the free coordinates read from $x$ — has decision-tree depth
exceeding $t$ is at most
\[
s\left(\tfrac12\right)^{l} + \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t} + s\,e^{-n/(120 l)} + e^{-n/(120
l)}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\uses{DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.cleanDNF, LMN.cleanDNF_eval, LMN.cleanDNF_nodup, LMN.cleanDNF_var_inj, LMN.cleanDNF_width_le, SwitchingLemma.Restriction, SwitchingLemma.dtDepth_le_implies_small_dnf_cnf, SwitchingLemma.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$, $m$, and $l$ be natural numbers, let $\rho_1$ be a restriction on $n$
variables, and let $g_1, \dots, g_m$ be DNF formulas on $n$ variables. For each $i$,
write $g_i|_{\rho_1}$ for the restricted Boolean function $x \mapsto
g_i\bigl(\rho_1.\mathrm{extend}\,x\bigr)$, that is, $g_i$ evaluated on the input
obtained by setting the fixed coordinates of $\rho_1$ and reading the free coordinates
from $x$. Suppose that for every $i$ the decision-tree depth of $g_i|_{\rho_1}$ is at
most $l$. Then there exist DNF formulas $g_1', \dots, g_m'$ such that, for every $i$:
the width of $g_i'$ is at most $l$; $g_i'$ computes $g_i|_{\rho_1}$ on every input;
within each term of $g_i'$ any two literals on the same variable are identical; and no
term of $g_i'$ contains a repeated literal.
\end{lemma}
